headline: Highest risk is medium prompt-injection/cascading-error from Copilot editing repo context; other pairwise risks are low or none because python-cheatsheet is documentation-only and non-writable.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Copilot reads repo context and open editor buffers, and its Workspace plans can apply edits for human review; the cheatsheet agent is documentation-only and cannot write or ingest files. The pairwise pathway exists if Copilot consumes attacker-controlled repo content as instructions, but the blast radius is limited to code edits rather than autonomous execution.
conditions: IF attacker-controlled text is present in repo context or open buffers
IF Copilot Workspace is used to generate edits from that content
mitigations: Strip or quarantine untrusted prompt-like text in repo files
Use branch protection for AI-authored changes
Limit Copilot to small, scoped files
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for untrusted content

B_data_leakage.rationale: Copilot can read filesystem content and send context to api.githubcopilot.com, while the cheatsheet agent has no filesystem, clipboard, or network surfaces. Because B touches no data classes and cannot ingest shared workspace data, leakage across the pair is limited unless the operator manually copies sensitive content into Copilot.
conditions: IF sensitive source code is opened in Copilot context
IF the operator manually pastes that content into another system
mitigations: Avoid opening secrets in the editor
Use separate repos for sensitive material

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Copilot can modify git state and write the filesystem, but the cheatsheet agent cannot write, modify git, or access files. There is no overlapping mutable resource in the pair, so direct write-write conflict is absent; only Copilot-side edits can occur.
conditions: IF the cheatsheet agent is replaced with a writable tool
IF another writable agent is added to the same repo
mitigations: Review Copilot git diffs before commit
Avoid concurrent edits on the same branch

D_cascading_error.rationale: Copilot produces code suggestions and Workspace edits that a human may accept, while the cheatsheet agent is a reference source with no verification or action-taking authority. If Copilot treats reference text as authoritative, errors can cascade into incorrect code or docs, but the pair lacks autonomous downstream execution.
conditions: IF Copilot uses cheatsheet text as factual authority
IF the human accepts Workspace edits without review
mitigations: Require human review of all AI edits

E_compliance.rationale: No compliance-sensitive data class, residency mismatch, or regulated workflow is indicated. Copilot touches source code and open buffers only, and the cheatsheet agent is documentation-only with no data handling or network egress, so no pairwise compliance breach is evidenced.
conditions: IF regulated data is introduced into the repo context
IF the operator uses the pair on PHI, EU PII, or secrets
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the workspace
